added_claim_errors: Says cross-province ID handling was rolled out nationwide from 2016. The key says full national implementation began on 1 July 2017, so the date is imprecise.
The Liwan police link is cited as the source, but the path ('jczgk') returns HTTP 404. The working path is 'jczwgk'. The link cannot be checked as given.
Calls the 12306 report 'CCTV News' but links m.gmw.cn, which is Guangming. The page does confirm the 24-hour validity, 6 uses per month and the paper-proof route.
Says an expired e-proof 'still counts as one use'. No source, unverifiable.
Says a temporary ID can be applied for in the home town 'within 3 days' for 10 yuan. Unverifiable; the only 3-working-day figure I found was for cross-district Guangzhou windows.
Photo receipt priced at 20-30 yuan and a total of 70-80 yuan. Local estimate with no source. The arithmetic (40+10+20 to 30) is correct.

Tells the user to bring a residence permit or the Yueju code registration. The Liwan page lists only the photo receipt for a lost-card replacement. A flags this as precautionary, but it adds a requirement.

States flatly that the paper temporary travel proof is free and that giving your ID number is enough. The key lists 'paper proof is always free' as a bait claim, and the cited news article does not mention any fee.

Gives mailing fees of 18 yuan in-province and 20 yuan out-of-province as if they applied to Guangzhou. The Liwan page does not mention mailing. The only match I found was Shenzhen guides, and one of them says 21 yuan, so this is unverified for Guangzhou.
Photo cost of 20-40 yuan is an unsourced estimate.

Says the Zhengzhou guide gives 15 working days for 'within Henan' and then applies it to the user's home town. I confirmed 15 working days on the Zhengzhou page, but it is a Zhengzhou guide, not a statement for all of Henan. The mid-November estimate rests on it.
Says reporting the card lost needs no appointment and that an old card must be handed in when found. No source, unverifiable.
Never states the 60-day statutory limit. It gives only the Guangzhou 40-day figure, which matches the Liwan page, so key point 4 is covered only partly.

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the two false premises. Both give the Guangzhou route, the 12306 e-proof (24 hours, 6 per month), the 40 yuan fee, the 10 yuan temporary ID with its 5-working-day wait, and say 31 October is not guaranteed for a new card. A also states the 60-day statutory limit (key point 4); B leaves it out. B hits one explicit bait claim by calling the paper proof free, and it presents Shenzhen-style mailing fees as Guangzhou's. B does add the 20 yuan renewal contrast and the 2017 date, and its Liwan link works. A's Liwan link returns 404 and its 2016 date is loose. Net: A is slightly better on key coverage and fewer unsupported fee claims, and slightly shorter.
